title: Louis Armstrong as chief influence; Busse and Red Nichols
summary: Scott says Armstrong influenced him most.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: If you were to name a musician, trumpet player or other musician, who influenced you the most, who would you --

Who influenced me the most? Well, the one that I got most influence from was Louis, Louis Armstrong. Because Louis and I got very close. And he style was so different and everybody would listen to him. I didn't try to imitate him because nobody can do Louis. He was just Louis and that was all.

But he told me about a lot of different things out West and all like that, and wasn't any particular trumpet player around at that time that -- Henry Busse, he worked with -- I knew him with Paul Whitman. He was Whitman's trumpet player. And then Red Nichols came along at that time, and he
worked at Roseland, he was a nice trumpet player. You know Red Nichols and his Five Pennies? They made a lot of records. I liked them both.
